$comment: The PUBLIC demo answer key, and the template to copy. `pnpm gen --sample` builds src/lib/generated/sample/ from this, which is what a fresh clone plays until someone runs `pnpm gen` with their own flags.secret.json. Two rules make it safe to publish. Every phrase here starts `demo_` and shares nothing with any real deployment's -- reusing a real phrase would hand out the readable half of a live flag, since the random suffix is the only part that differs. And hints and writeups are empty, because the real ones would spoil every deployment rather than just this demo. To start your own: copy this file to flags.secret.json, replace every phrase, and add your own hints and writeups.

honeypots.pctf{n1ce_try_but_no}: That one is printed on the front page as an example. Flags that want to be found aren't flags.
honeypots.pctf{grep_is_not_a_solution}: Found in a source comment, was it? Comments are where developers put things they've stopped thinking about.
honeypots.pctf{th4ts_a_decoy_friend}: A cookie literally named `flag`. Plausible is doing a lot of work in that sentence.
honeypots.pctf{x_marks_the_header}: A response header called X-Flag. If it were that easy, the trophy would be made of cardboard.
